   118	variable {d : ℕ}
   119	
   120	/-! ### Definitions -/
   121	
   122	/-- The supplied input for `N₀`: the mass identity `G_s(ℝ^d) = s` for `s > 0`
   123	(proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, line 825), stated for a family `G` of
   124	measures on `ℝ^d` standing for the wave Green measures, which this package
   125	does not define. -/
   126	structure GreenMass (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) : Prop where
   127	  mass : ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → G s univ = ENNReal.ofReal s
   128	
   129	/-- `N₀(θ) = ∫_0^∞ e^{-θs} G_s(ℝ^d) ds` (`E:damped-norm-definitions`, line 747),
   130	for a family `G` of measures on `ℝ^d`. -/
   131	def N0 (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) (θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   132	  ∫ s in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Real.exp (-(θ * s)) * (G s univ).toReal
   133	
   134	/-- The first norm with the Laplace variable restricted to `S`:
   135	`Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} λ^{a-1} R_Γ(θ+λ) dλ`. -/
   136	def N1on (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ :=
   137	  (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * ∫ l in S, l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l) ∂L0
   138	
   139	/-- `N₁^{(M)}(1)`, the first norm at `θ = 1` with `λ > M` (lines 782-784). -/
   140	def N1tail (a M : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ := N1on a 1 (Ioi M) μ
   141	
   142	/-- The temporal kernel with the Laplace variable restricted to `S`:
   143	`K_S(r) = Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} e^{-λ|r|} λ^{a-1} dλ`.  At `r = 0` with
   144	`S ∩ (0,∞)` of infinite `λ^{a-1} dλ`-mass the integral diverges and the Lean
   145	value is the junk value `0`; this happens only on the diagonal `s = t`, a
   146	`P2`-null set. -/
   147	def KS (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   148	  (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * ∫ l in S, subKernel a |r| l ∂L0
   149	
   150	/-- `K_M(r) = Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_M^∞ e^{-λ|r|} λ^{a-1} dλ` (lines 778-781), the
   151	`λ`-integral taken over `(M,∞) ∩ (0,∞)`. -/
   152	def KM (a M r : ℝ) : ℝ := KS a (Ioi M) r
   153	
   154	/-- The outer integrand of the second norm with kernel `K_S`. -/
   155	def N2onOuter (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ :=
   156	  Real.exp (-(θ * (p.1 + p.2))) * KS a S (p.1 - p.2) *
   157	    ∫ ξ, waveHat p.1 ξ * waveHat p.2 ξ ∂μ
   158	
   159	/-- The integrand on `(0,∞)² × ℝ^d` of the second norm with kernel `K_S`. -/
   160	def N2onIntegrand (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (z : (ℝ × ℝ) × Rd d) : ℝ :=
   161	  Real.exp (-(θ * (z.1.1 + z.1.2))) * KS a S (z.1.1 - z.1.2) *
   162	    (waveHat z.1.1 z.2 * waveHat z.1.2 z.2)
   163	
   164	/-- The squared second norm with `K_S(s-t)` in place of `|s-t|^{-a}`. -/
   165	def N2onSq (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ :=
   166	  ∫ p, N2onOuter a θ S μ p ∂P2
   167	
   168	/-- `N₂^{(M)}(1)²`: the squared second norm at `θ = 1` with `K_M(s-t)` in place
   169	of `|s-t|^{-a}` (lines 783-784). -/
   170	def N2tailSq (a M : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ := N2onSq a 1 (Ioi M) μ
   171	
   172	/-- `N₂^{(M)}(1) = (N₂^{(M)}(1)²)^{1/2}` (the printed form of `E:damped-tail-norms`). -/
   173	def N2tail (a M : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (N2tailSq a M μ)
   174	
   175	/-- The spectral measure multiplied by `g`, `g(ξ) μ(dξ)` (the reading of
   176	"Gaussian smoothing" adopted for lines 789-791; that `g` is measurable with
   177	values in `[0,1]` is imposed separately). -/
   178	def smoothed (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) : Measure (Rd d) :=
   179	  μ.withDensity fun ξ => (g ξ : ℝ≥0∞)
   180	
   181	/-- The subordinated integrand `FK` restricted to `λ ∈ S` (auxiliary to the Lean
   182	proof route). -/
   183	def FKS (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) : ℝ × (Rd d × (ℝ × ℝ)) → ℝ :=
   184	  (Prod.fst ⁻¹' S).indicator (FK a θ)

   188	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. `α > 0` under `H:homog`. -/
   189	theorem alpha_pos {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}

   191	  rcases h.alpha_range with h1 | h1
   192	  · exact h1.1
   193	  · rw [h1.1, h1.2]; norm_num
   194	
   195	/-- `0 ≤ K_S(r)` (line 832 for `S = (M,∞)`). -/
   196	theorem KS_nonneg (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (r : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) : 0 ≤ KS a S r := by
   197	  have := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha
   198	  refine mul_nonneg (by positivity) (integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_)
   199	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   200	  exact subKernel_nonneg a |r| l hl.le

   202	/-- `K_S(r) ≤ |r|^{-a}` for `r ≠ 0` (lines 832-833 for `S = (M,∞)`), with the
   203	`λ`-integral integrable. -/
   204	theorem KS_le (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (r : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hr : r ≠ 0) :
   205	    IntegrableOn (subKernel a |r|) S L0 ∧ KS a S r ≤ |r| ^ (-a) := by

   207	  have hI := subKernel_integrable a |r| ha hr'
   208	  refine ⟨hI.integrableOn, ?_⟩
   209	  rw [rpow_neg_eq_subordination a |r| ha hr', KS]
   210	  have := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha
   211	  refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (setIntegral_le_integral hI ?_) (by positivity)
   212	  filter_upwards [ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   213	  exact subKernel_nonneg a |r| l hl.le
   214	
   215	/-- `K_{(0,∞)}(r) = |r|^{-a}` for `r ≠ 0`. -/
   216	theorem KS_univ (a r : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hr : r ≠ 0) : KS a univ r = |r| ^ (-a) := by
   217	  rw [rpow_neg_eq_subordination a |r| ha (abs_pos.2 hr), KS, Measure.restrict_univ]

   219	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. Tails of an integrable function on `(0,∞)`
   220	tend to `0`. -/
   221	theorem tail_tendsto_zero {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f L0) :
   222	    Tendsto (fun M : ℝ => ∫ l in Ioi M, f l ∂L0) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
   223	  have h := tendsto_setIntegral_of_antitone (μ := L0) (f := f) (s := fun M : ℝ => Ioi M)
   224	    (fun _ => measurableSet_Ioi) (fun _ _ hMN => Ioi_subset_Ioi hMN) ⟨0, hf.integrableOn⟩
   225	  have he : (⋂ M : ℝ, Ioi M) = ∅ := by
   226	    ext x
   227	    simp only [mem_iInter, mem_Ioi, mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_forall, not_lt]
   228	    exact ⟨x, le_rfl⟩
   229	  rwa [he, Measure.restrict_empty, integral_zero_measure] at h

   231	/-- `K_M(r) → 0` as `M → ∞` for `r ≠ 0` (line 833). -/
   232	theorem KM_tendsto (a r : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hr : r ≠ 0) :

   234	  have hI := subKernel_integrable a |r| ha (abs_pos.2 hr)
   235	  simpa [KM, KS] using (tail_tendsto_zero hI).const_mul (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹

   238	
   239	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. Scaling of the weight `w_θ` of
   240	`ClockCopy`: `w_θ(θu) = θ^{a+α-5} w_1(u)` for `θ, u > 0`, given the spectral

241	homogeneity `μ(cA) = c^α μ(A)`. -/
   242	theorem weight_scaling {μ : Measure (Rd d)} {alpha : ℝ} (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha)
   243	    (a θ u : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hu : 0 < u) :
   244	    weight a θ μ (θ * u) = θ ^ (a + alpha - 5) * weight a 1 μ u := by
   245	  unfold weight
   246	  rw [show θ + θ * u = θ * (1 + u) by ring]
   247	  rw [resolvent_homog hI θ hθ, resolvent_homog hI (θ * (1 + u)) (by positivity),
   248	    resolvent_homog hI (1 + u) (by positivity), resolvent_homog hI 1 one_pos, Real.one_rpow,
   249	    one_mul, Real.mul_rpow hθ.le (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 + u by positivity),
   250	    Real.mul_rpow hθ.le hu.le]
   251	  have e : θ ^ (a + alpha - 5) = θ ^ (a - 2) * θ ^ (alpha - 2) * θ⁻¹ := by
   252	    rw [← Real.rpow_add hθ, ← Real.rpow_neg_one, ← Real.rpow_add hθ]; ring_nf
   253	  rw [e]
   254	  field_simp

   256	/-- `N₂(θ)² = θ^{-β} N₂(1)²` with `β = 4 - α - α₀`, for `θ > 0`, under
   257	`H:homog` (lines 772-775; the change of variables of lines 825-829). -/
   258	theorem N2sq_scaling {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   259	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   260	    N2sq alpha0 θ μ = θ ^ (-(4 - alpha - alpha0)) * N2sq alpha0 1 μ := by

   173	\section{Model and standing assumptions}\label{S:model}
   174	
   175	We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
   176	\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
   177	\begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
   178	  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
   179	  \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
   180	\end{equation}
   181	for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
   182	Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
   183	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   184	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   185	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   186	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
   187	\end{equation}
   188	where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
   189	
   190	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   191	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   192	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   193	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   194	  convention
   195	  \[
   196	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   197	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   198	  \]
   199	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   200	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   201	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   202	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   203	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   204	  \end{equation}
   205	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   206	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   207	\end{hypothesis}
   208	
   209	\paragraph{Zero covariance.}
   210	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} allows $\Gamma = 0$ by design. In this case the
   211	centered Gaussian noise is $\W = 0$, and the solution with initial data
   212	$(1,0)$ is $u(t,x) = 1$. Thus $\E|u(t,x)|^p = 1$ for every $p > 0$, and
   213	all normalized logarithmic moment rates are zero. Results asserting strict
   214	positivity of covariance-dependent quantities impose $\Gamma \ne 0$ locally.
   215

   738	\section{Recovering the quadratic-exponential bound}
   739	
   740	Write $G_\theta(s,y) = e^{-\theta s}G(s,y)$ and $\widehat{G}_s(\xi) =
   741	\sin(s|\xi|)/|\xi|$, with value $s$ at $\xi = 0$. We use the norms in the
   742	source's (3.3)--(3.5), with the full covariance, but give their bounds directly.
   743	Write $\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}$ for Euler's Gamma function in the following
   744	definitions, to distinguish it from the covariance measure:
   745	\begin{equation}\label{E:damped-norm-definitions}
   746	  \begin{split}
   747	    N_0(\theta)&=\int_0^\infty e^{-\theta s}G_s(\R^d)\ud s,\\
   748	    N_1(\theta)&=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   749	    \int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda
   750	    \int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{(\theta+\lambda)^2+|\xi|^2},\\
   751	    N_2(\theta)^2&=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   752	    e^{-\theta(s+t)}|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}
   753	    \int\widehat{G}_s(\xi)\overline{\widehat{G}_t(\xi)}
   754	    \mu(\ud\xi)\ud s\ud t.
   755	  \end{split}
   756	\end{equation}
   757	The second expression uses the elementary wave Laplace transform $\int_0^\infty
   758	e^{-as}\widehat{G}_s(\xi)\ud s = (a^2+|\xi|^2)^{-1}$. The last expression is the
   759	space-time covariance quadratic form; in physical variables it pairs
   760	$G_\theta(s,x)$ with $G_\theta(t,y)$. Thus, the second Green factor in the
   761	printed source (3.5) is read with the independent variable $y$; see
   762	Lemma~\ref{L:translated-covariance-CS} and
   763	Remark~\ref{R:source-case2-time-shift} for the independent justification and the
   764	exact source qualification.
   765	
   766	\begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
   767	  \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
   768	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
   769	  in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
   770	  $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
   771	  \[
   772	    N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
   773	    N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
   774	    N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
   775	    \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
   776	  \]
   777	  Let
   778	  \[
   779	    K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   780	    \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   781	  \]
   782	  Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
   783	  $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   784	  $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   785	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   786	    N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   787	    N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   788	  \end{equation}
   789	  Spatial Gaussian smoothing, Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel, and
   790	  restriction of a temporal Laplace domain do not increase these corresponding
   791	  full or tail norm bounds.
   792	\end{lemma}
   793	
   794	\begin{proof}
   795	  Scaling the Fourier representation of $\Gamma$ and using Fourier uniqueness
   796	  gives $\mu(cA) = c^\alpha\mu(A)$. Radon finiteness and $\alpha > 0$ then imply
   797	  $\mu(\{0\}) = 0$. In particular, $\mu(B_r) = r^\alpha V$, where $V = \mu(B_1)
   798	  < \infty$. Therefore, for $a > 0$,
   799	  \[
   800	    \int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{a^2+|\xi|^2}
   801	    =\alpha V a^{\alpha-2}
   802	    \int_0^\infty\frac{u^{\alpha-1}}{1+u^2}\ud u<\infty.
   803	  \]
   804	  The last integral is finite since $0 < \alpha < 2$. Substitution into $N_1$
   805	  reduces its finiteness to
   806	  $\int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}(\theta+\lambda)^{\alpha-2} \ud\lambda <
   807	  \infty$: the conditions at zero and infinity are $\alpha_0 > 0$ and
   808	  $\alpha+\alpha_0 < 2$.
   809	
   810	  For $N_2$ use $|\widehat{G}_s(\xi)| \le \min(s,|\xi|^{-1})$. On $|\xi| \le 1$,
   811	  absolute integration is bounded by
   812	  \[
   813	    V\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   814	    e^{-\theta(s+t)}|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}st\ud s\ud t<\infty.
   815	  \]
   816	  On $|\xi| > 1$, use $\int_{|\xi|>1}|\xi|^{-2}\mu(\ud\xi) = \alpha
   817	  V/(2-\alpha)$ and the same time integral without $st$. Both time integrals are
   818	  finite by splitting into $s \le t$ and $t \le s$, then using $u = \min(s,t)$
   819	  and $v = |s-t|$; the only singular factor is $v^{-\alpha_0}$, with $\alpha_0 <
   820	  1$. This proves absolute integrability of the displayed spectral formula. For
   821	  each $\xi$, its time integral is nonnegative because the temporal kernel is
   822	  positive definite. Indeed, it is a positive Laplace mixture of the kernels
   823	  $e^{-\lambda|s-t|}$. This proves $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$.
   824	
   825	  The mass identity $G_s(\R^d) = s$ proves the formula for $N_0$. In $N_1$
   826	  change $\lambda = \theta u$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$. In $N_2$ change $s =
   827	  u/\theta$, $t = v/\theta$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$, using
   828	  $\widehat{G}_{u/\theta}(\theta\eta) = \theta^{-1}\widehat{G}_u(\eta)$. These
   829	  changes give exactly the stated powers.
   830	
   831	  The first tail in~\eqref{E:damped-tail-norms} is a tail of the finite
   832	  nonnegative $N_1(1)$ integral. For the second, $0 \le K_M(r) \le
   833	  |r|^{-\alpha_0}$ and $K_M(r) \to 0$ for $r \ne 0$. The absolute majorant just
   834	  proved permits dominated convergence in $(s,t,\xi)$, giving $N_2^{(M)}(1)^2
   835	  \to 0$. The tail kernel is positive definite by the same Laplace-mixture
   836	  argument, so its quadratic form is nonnegative.
   837	
   838	  Spatial and Green Gaussian smoothing multiply the spectral integrals by
   839	  factors in $[0,1]$. For $N_1$ the integrand is nonnegative. For $N_2$, first
   840	  integrate in time: the quadratic form at each $\xi$ is nonnegative, so its
   841	  Gaussian multiplier can be removed in an upper bound. Restricting a temporal
   842	  Laplace domain likewise decreases the first norm and its nonnegative
   843	  covariance quadratic form. This proves all smoothing and truncation
   844	  assertions, including the bounds for temporal tails. This proves
   845	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}.
   846	\end{proof}
   847	
   848	\paragraph{Covariance pairings of translated kernels.}
   849	Fix $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. Let $\mu$ be a finite positive Borel measure on $\R^d$
   850	such that $\gamma(z) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}\mu(\ud\xi)$ is real and nonnegative
   851	for every $z$. Thus, $\gamma$ is bounded, continuous and even, with $0 \le
   852	\gamma(z) \le \mu(\R^d)$. Let $\nu$ be a positive Borel measure on $(0,\infty)$
   853	with $\nu((0,L]) < \infty$ for every $L > 0$, and put
   854	\[
   855	  \kappa_L(t)=\int_{(0,L]}e^{-\lambda|t|}\nu(\ud\lambda),\qquad
   856	  C_L((t,x),(s,y))=\kappa_L(t-s)\gamma(x-y).
   857	\]
   858	For complex $L^1(\R\times\R^d)$ functions $f,h$, define
   859	\begin{equation}\label{E:translated-covariance-form}
   860	  Q_L(f,h)=\int_{\R^2}\int_{\R^{2d}}
   861	  f(t,x)\overline{h(s,y)}\kappa_L(t-s)\gamma(x-y)
   862	  \ud x\ud y\ud t\ud s.
   863	\end{equation}
   864	This integral is absolutely convergent, with $|Q_L(f,h)| \le
   865	\nu((0,L])\mu(\R^d)\|f\|_1\|h\|_1$. For nonnegative $f,h$, define $Q(f,h) =
   866	\lim_{L\to\infty}Q_L(f,h)$ as an extended nonnegative number. This positive cap
   867	limit also defines the pairing when the full temporal kernel is singular on the
   868	diagonal. The spatial covariance is fixed throughout this definition. For a
   869	nonnegative Borel function $G$ on $(0,\infty)\times\R^d$, let $G^0$ be its zero
   870	extension to nonpositive times and put
   871	\[
   872	  N_0(G)=\int_0^\infty\int_{\R^d}G(t,x)\ud x\ud t,\qquad
   873	  N_C(G)^2=Q(G^0,G^0).
   874	\]
   875	For $(A,a) \in \R\times\R^d$, write $T_{A,a}f(t,x) = f(t-A,x-a)$. All translated
   876	pairings are over the full time line.

   878	\begin{lemma}[Translated covariance Cauchy--Schwarz]
   879	  \label{L:translated-covariance-CS}
   880	  Under the preceding assumptions on $\mu$ and $\nu$, let $G_1,G_2$ be
   881	  nonnegative Borel functions with $N_0(G_i),N_C(G_i) < \infty$, $i = 1,2$. For
   882	  arbitrary origins $(A,a),(B,b) \in \R\times\R^d$,
   883	  \begin{equation}\label{E:translated-covariance-CS}
   884	    0\le Q(T_{A,a}G_1^0,T_{B,b}G_2^0)\le N_C(G_1)N_C(G_2),
   885	  \end{equation}
   886	  and $Q(T_{A,a}G_i^0,T_{A,a}G_i^0) = N_C(G_i)^2$ for $i = 1,2$. The coefficient
   887	  one is independent of the origins, dimension, cap and covariance masses. Zero
   888	  norms and zero measures are included.
   889	\end{lemma}

    88	/-- `w_θ(λ) = λ^{a-2}/(2θΓ(a)) (R_Γ(θ) - R_Γ(θ+λ))`
    89	(`E:cross-clock-lambda-weight`, lines 7683-7689). -/
    90	def weight (a θ : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (l : ℝ) : ℝ :=
    91	  l ^ (a - 2) / (2 * θ * Real.Gamma a) * (𝓡 μ θ - 𝓡 μ (θ + l))
    92	
    93	/-- The integrand `2θ/(2θ+λ) w_θ(λ)` of `J_{Γ,1}` in `E:clock-copy-obstruction`. -/
    94	def filteredWeight (a θ : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (l : ℝ) : ℝ :=
    95	  2 * θ / (2 * θ + l) * weight a θ μ l
    96	
    97	/-- `v_ρ(u,v) = u + v - 2ρ min(u,v)` (line 7664). -/
    98	def vRho (ρ u v : ℝ) : ℝ := u + v - 2 * ρ * min u v

   100	/-- The integrand of `E:naive-clock-candidate`:
   101	`e^{-θ²(u+v)/2} h_Γ(u+v) Ψ_a(θ|u-v|, v_ρ(u,v))`. -/
   102	def Jintegrand (a θ : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (ρ : ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ :=
   103	  Real.exp (-(θ ^ 2 * (p.1 + p.2) / 2)) * heat μ (p.1 + p.2) *
   104	    Psi a (θ * |p.1 - p.2|) (vRho ρ p.1 p.2)
   105	
   106	/-- `J_{Γ,ρ}(θ)` of `E:naive-clock-candidate` (lines 7668-7673). -/
   107	def J (a θ : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (ρ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   108	  1 / 4 * ∫ p, Jintegrand a θ μ ρ p ∂P2
   109	
   110	/-- The subordinated integrand of `J_{Γ,1}` on `(0,∞) × ℝ^d × (0,∞)²`
   111	(auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   112	def FJ (a θ : ℝ) (z : ℝ × (Rd d × (ℝ × ℝ))) : ℝ :=
   113	  1 / 4 * (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * |z.1| ^ (a - 1) *
   114	    twoTimeR ((θ ^ 2 + ‖z.2.1‖ ^ 2) / 2) (θ * |z.1| + |z.1| ^ 2 / 2) z.2.2

   118	/-- `v_1(u,v) = |u-v|` (line 7771). -/
   119	theorem vRho_one (u v : ℝ) : vRho 1 u v = |u - v| := by
   120	  unfold vRho
   121	  rcases le_total u v with h | h
   122	  · rw [min_eq_left h, abs_of_nonpos (by linarith)]; ring
   123	  · rw [min_eq_right h, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]; ring
   124	
   125	/-- `v_ρ(u,v) ≥ |u-v|` for `ρ ≤ 1`, `u, v ≥ 0` (line 7771). -/
   126	theorem abs_le_vRho (ρ u v : ℝ) (hρ : ρ ≤ 1) (hu : 0 ≤ u) (hv : 0 ≤ v) :
   127	    |u - v| ≤ vRho ρ u v := by
   128	  rw [← vRho_one]
   129	  unfold vRho
   130	  have : 0 ≤ min u v := le_min hu hv
   131	  nlinarith

   164	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. Partial fractions: `1/(AB) = (1/A - 1/B)/(λ(2θ+λ))` with
   165	`A = θ²+r²`,
   166	`B = (θ+λ)²+r²`. -/
   167	theorem inv_mul_partial (θ l r : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hl : 0 < l) :
   168	    1 / ((θ ^ 2 + r ^ 2) * ((θ + l) ^ 2 + r ^ 2)) =
   169	      1 / (l * (2 * θ + l)) * (1 / (θ ^ 2 + r ^ 2) - 1 / ((θ + l) ^ 2 + r ^ 2)) := by
   170	  have hA : θ ^ 2 + r ^ 2 ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (by positivity)
   171	  have hB : (θ + l) ^ 2 + r ^ 2 ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (by positivity)
   172	  have hC : l * (2 * θ + l) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (by positivity)
   173	  field_simp
   174	  ring

   176	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   177	theorem resolvent_le (μ : Measure (Rd d))
   178	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ)
   179	    (q q' : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hqq : q ≤ q') : 𝓡 μ q' ≤ 𝓡 μ q := by
   180	  refine integral_mono (resolvent_integrable hR q' (by linarith))
   181	    (resolvent_integrable hR q hq.ne') fun ξ => ?_
   182	  have : 0 < q ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 := by positivity
   183	  exact one_div_le_one_div_of_le this (by nlinarith)

   185	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. `R_Γ(θ) - R_Γ(θ+λ) ≤ λ(2θ+λ)θ⁻² R_Γ(θ)`. -/
   186	theorem resolvent_sub_le (μ : Measure (Rd d))
   187	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (θ l : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ)
   188	    (hl : 0 < l) :
   189	    𝓡 μ θ - 𝓡 μ (θ + l) ≤ l * (2 * θ + l) / θ ^ 2 * 𝓡 μ θ := by
   190	  unfold SpectralHomog.resolvent
   191	  have h1 := resolvent_integrable hR θ hθ.ne'
   192	  have h2 := resolvent_integrable hR (θ + l) (by linarith)
   193	  rw [← integral_sub h1 h2, ← integral_const_mul]
   194	  refine integral_mono (h1.sub h2) (h1.const_mul _) fun ξ => ?_
   195	  have hA : 0 < θ ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 := by positivity
   196	  have hB : 0 < (θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 := by positivity
   197	  have e : 1 / (θ ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) - 1 / ((θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) =
   198	      l * (2 * θ + l) / ((θ ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) * ((θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   199	    field_simp; ring
   200	  simp only
   201	  rw [e, mul_one_div, div_div, div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)]
   202	  have hn : 0 ≤ l * (2 * θ + l) := by positivity
   203	  have : θ ^ 2 ≤ (θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg ‖ξ‖]
   204	  have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left this (mul_nonneg hn hA.le)
   205	  nlinarith

   237	/-- `w_θ` is integrable on `(0,∞)`. -/
   238	theorem weight_integrable (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   239	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a)
   240	    (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) : Integrable (weight a θ μ) L0 := by
   241	  have hG := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha0
   242	  have hR0 := resolvent_nonneg μ θ
   243	  set D := 2 * θ * Real.Gamma a
   244	  have hD : 0 < D := by positivity
   245	  refine integrable_of_rpow_bounds (a - 1) (a - 2)
   246	    ((2 * θ + 1) / θ ^ 2 * 𝓡 μ θ / D + 𝓡 μ θ / D) (by linarith) (by linarith)
   247	    (weight_measurable μ a θ).aestronglyMeasurable ?_ ?_
   248	  · intro l hl hl1
   249	    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (weight_nonneg μ hR a θ l ha0 hθ hl)]
   250	    have hs := resolvent_sub_le μ hR θ l hθ hl
   251	    have hp : l ^ (a - 1) = l ^ (a - 2) * l := by
   252	      rw [show a - 1 = (a - 2) + 1 by ring, Real.rpow_add_one hl.ne']
   253	    have hq := Real.rpow_nonneg hl.le (a - 2)
   254	    unfold weight
   255	    rw [hp]
   256	    have h1 : l * (2 * θ + l) / θ ^ 2 * 𝓡 μ θ ≤
   257	        l * ((2 * θ + 1) / θ ^ 2 * 𝓡 μ θ) := by
   258	      rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_mul_eq_mul_div, mul_div_assoc', div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right
   259	        (by positivity)]
   260	      have : 2 * θ + l ≤ 2 * θ + 1 := by linarith
   261	      nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left this (mul_nonneg hl.le hR0)]
   262	    have h2 := hs.trans h1
   263	    have h3 : 0 ≤ 𝓡 μ θ / D := div_nonneg hR0 hD.le
   264	    calc l ^ (a - 2) / D * (𝓡 μ θ - 𝓡 μ (θ + l))
   265	        ≤ l ^ (a - 2) / D * (l * ((2 * θ + 1) / θ ^ 2 * 𝓡 μ θ)) :=
   266	          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h2 (by positivity)
   267	      _ = (2 * θ + 1) / θ ^ 2 * 𝓡 μ θ / D * (l ^ (a - 2) * l) := by ring
   268	      _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (le_add_of_nonneg_right h3) (by positivity)
   269	  · intro l hl
   270	    have hl0 : 0 < l := lt_trans zero_lt_one hl
   271	    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (weight_nonneg μ hR a θ l ha0 hθ hl0)]
   272	    have hR1 := resolvent_nonneg μ (θ + l)
   273	    have hq := Real.rpow_nonneg hl0.le (a - 2)
   274	    unfold weight
   275	    have h0 : 0 ≤ (2 * θ + 1) / θ ^ 2 * 𝓡 μ θ / D := by positivity
   276	    calc l ^ (a - 2) / D * (𝓡 μ θ - 𝓡 μ (θ + l))
   277	        ≤ l ^ (a - 2) / D * 𝓡 μ θ :=
   278	          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (by linarith) (by positivity)
   279	      _ = 𝓡 μ θ / D * l ^ (a - 2) := by ring
   280	      _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (le_add_of_nonneg_left h0) hq

   284	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a)
   285	    (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) : Integrable (filteredWeight a θ μ) L0 := by

   287	    ((by fun_prop : Measurable fun l : ℝ => 2 * θ / (2 * θ + l)).mul

   292	  rw [filteredWeight, Real.norm_of_nonneg (mul_nonneg hb.1.le hw)]

   297	/-- `∫ Γ(a)⁻¹λ^{a-1}/((θ²+|ξ|²)((θ+λ)²+|ξ|²)) μ(dξ) = 2θ/(2θ+λ) w_θ(λ)`. -/
   298	theorem xi_integral_J (μ : Measure (Rd d))
   299	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (a θ l : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ)
   300	    (hl : 0 < l) :
   301	    Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * l ^ (a - 1) /
   302	        ((θ ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) * ((θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2))) μ ∧
   303	      ∫ ξ, (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * l ^ (a - 1) /
   304	          ((θ ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) * ((θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) ∂μ =
   305	        filteredWeight a θ μ l := by
   306	  have h1 := resolvent_integrable hR θ hθ.ne'
   307	  have h2 := resolvent_integrable hR (θ + l) (by linarith)
   308	  have hpt : (fun ξ : Rd d => (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * l ^ (a - 1) /
   309	      ((θ ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) * ((θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2))) = fun ξ =>
   310	      ((Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * l ^ (a - 1) * (1 / (l * (2 * θ + l)))) *
   311	        (1 / (θ ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) - 1 / ((θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   312	    funext ξ
   313	    rw [mul_assoc, ← inv_mul_partial θ l ‖ξ‖ hθ hl]
   314	    ring
   315	  rw [hpt]
   316	  refine ⟨(h1.sub h2).const_mul _, ?_⟩
   317	  rw [integral_const_mul, integral_sub h1 h2]
   318	  unfold filteredWeight weight SpectralHomog.resolvent
   319	  have hp : l ^ (a - 1) = l ^ (a - 2) * l := by
   320	    rw [show a - 1 = (a - 2) + 1 by ring, Real.rpow_add_one hl.ne']
   321	  rw [hp]
   322	  rcases eq_or_ne (Real.Gamma a) 0 with hG | hG
   323	  · simp [hG]
   324	  · field_simp

   347	/-! ### The cross transform at fixed `(λ, ξ)` -/
   348	
   349	/-- The first display of the proof of `P:clock-copy-obstruction` (lines
   350	7714-7720): for
   351	`ξ ≠ 0`, `λ ≥ 0`, `θ > 0`,
   352	`∫∫ e^{-θ(s+t)-λ|s-t|} Ĝ_s(ξ) Ĝ_t(ξ) ds dt
   353	  = (2θ+λ)/(2θ(θ²+|ξ|²)((θ+λ)²+|ξ|²))`. -/
   354	theorem cross_transform (θ l : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hl : 0 ≤ l) (ξ : Rd d) (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) :
   355	    Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => twoTimeR θ l p * (waveHat p.1 ξ * waveHat p.2 ξ)) P2 ∧
   356	      ∫ p, twoTimeR θ l p * (waveHat p.1 ξ * waveHat p.2 ξ) ∂P2 =
   357	        (2 * θ + l) / (2 * θ * (θ ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) * ((θ + l) ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   358	  set r := ‖ξ‖ with hr_def
   359	  have hr : 0 < r := norm_pos_iff.2 hξ
   360	  set a1 : ℂ := (θ : ℂ) - (r : ℂ) * Complex.I
   361	  set b1 : ℂ := (θ : ℂ) + (r : ℂ) * Complex.I
   362	  have ha1 : 0 < a1.re := by simp [a1, hθ]
   363	  have hb1 : 0 < b1.re := by simp [b1, hθ]
   364	  obtain ⟨hC1, hV1⟩ := twoTimeC_integral a1 b1 l ha1 hb1 hl
   365	  obtain ⟨hC2, hV2⟩ := twoTimeC_integral a1 a1 l ha1 ha1 hl
   366	  have hpt : ∀ p : ℝ × ℝ, twoTimeR θ l p * (waveHat p.1 ξ * waveHat p.2 ξ) =
   367	      1 / (2 * r ^ 2) * (twoTimeC a1 b1 l p - twoTimeC a1 a1 l p).re := by
   368	    intro p
   369	    rw [waveHat_of_ne_zero _ _ hξ, waveHat_of_ne_zero _ _ hξ, ← hr_def, Complex.sub_re]
   370	    simp only [twoTimeC, Complex.exp_re]
   371	    have e1 : (-(a1 * (p.1 : ℂ)) - b1 * (p.2 : ℂ) -
   372	        (l : ℂ) * ((|p.1 - p.2| : ℝ) : ℂ)).re =
   373	        -(θ * (p.1 + p.2)) - l * |p.1 - p.2| := by simp [a1, b1]; ring
   374	    have e2 : (-(a1 * (p.1 : ℂ)) - b1 * (p.2 : ℂ) -
   375	        (l : ℂ) * ((|p.1 - p.2| : ℝ) : ℂ)).im =
   376	        p.1 * r - p.2 * r := by simp [a1, b1]; ring
   377	    have e3 : (-(a1 * (p.1 : ℂ)) - a1 * (p.2 : ℂ) -
   378	        (l : ℂ) * ((|p.1 - p.2| : ℝ) : ℂ)).re =
   379	        -(θ * (p.1 + p.2)) - l * |p.1 - p.2| := by simp [a1]; ring
   380	    have e4 : (-(a1 * (p.1 : ℂ)) - a1 * (p.2 : ℂ) -
   381	        (l : ℂ) * ((|p.1 - p.2| : ℝ) : ℂ)).im =
   382	        p.1 * r + p.2 * r := by simp [a1]; ring
   383	    rw [e1, e2, e3, e4, twoTimeR, Real.cos_sub, Real.cos_add]

   715	`Γ`, `θ > 0`, `-1 ≤ ρ ≤ 1`, and the supplied spectral homogeneity of `μ`
   716	(derived in the TeX proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`).  Conclusions:
   717	`w_θ` is a positive integrable density on `(0,∞)`; `K_Γ(θ) = N₂(θ)² = ∫ w_θ`
   718	(with integrable outer integrand); the candidate integrands are integrable
   719	and `0 < J_{Γ,ρ}(θ) ≤ J_{Γ,1}(θ) = ∫ 2θ/(2θ+λ) w_θ < K_Γ(θ)`
   720	(`E:clock-copy-obstruction`); and `J_{Γ,1}(θ) = (2-2^a) K_Γ(θ)` when `α = 1`
   721	(`E:degree-one-clock-loss`). -/
   722	theorem clock_copy_obstruction_paper {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   723	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha)
   724	    (hΓ : Γ ≠ 0) (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) (ρ : ℝ) (hρ : -1 ≤ ρ ∧ ρ ≤ 1) :
   725	    (∀ l : ℝ, 0 < l → 0 < weight alpha0 θ μ l) ∧ Integrable (weight alpha0 θ μ) L0 ∧
   726	      Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => Real.exp (-(θ * (p.1 + p.2))) * |p.1 - p.2| ^ (-alpha0) *
   727	        ∫ ξ, waveHat p.1 ξ * waveHat p.2 ξ ∂μ) P2 ∧
   728	      N2sq alpha0 θ μ = ∫ l in Ioi (0 : ℝ), weight alpha0 θ μ l ∧
   729	      Integrable (Jintegrand alpha0 θ μ ρ) P2 ∧ Integrable (Jintegrand alpha0 θ μ 1) P2 ∧
   730	      0 < J alpha0 θ μ ρ ∧ J alpha0 θ μ ρ ≤ J alpha0 θ μ 1 ∧
   731	      Integrable (filteredWeight alpha0 θ μ) L0 ∧
   732	      J alpha0 θ μ 1 = ∫ l in Ioi (0 : ℝ), filteredWeight alpha0 θ μ l ∧
   733	      J alpha0 θ μ 1 < N2sq alpha0 θ μ ∧
   734	      (alpha = 1 → J alpha0 θ μ 1 = (2 - 2 ^ alpha0) * N2sq alpha0 θ μ) := by
   735	  have := h.μ_radon
   736	  have := h.Γ_radon
   737	  have ha0 := h.alpha0_pos
   738	  have ha1 := h.alpha0_lt_one
   739	  have hα0 : 0 < alpha := by
   740	    rcases h.alpha_range with h1 | h1
   741	    · exact h1.1
   742	    · rw [h1.1, h1.2]; norm_num
   743	  have hα2 : alpha < 2 := by linarith [h.threshold]
   744	  have hR := integrable_inv_one_add_sq hI hα2
   745	  have hμ0 := measure_zero hI hα0
   746	  have hμ := spectral_ne_zero Γ μ h.spectral hΓ
   747	  have hK := K_eq_integral_weight μ hR hμ0 alpha0 θ ha0 ha1 hθ
   748	  obtain ⟨hJ1i, hJ1⟩ := J_one_eq μ hR alpha0 θ ha0 ha1 hθ
   749	  obtain ⟨hJi, hJpos, hJle⟩ := J_rho_props μ hR hμ alpha0 θ ρ ha0 ha1 hθ hρ.2
   750	  have hwi := weight_integrable μ hR alpha0 θ ha0 ha1 hθ
   751	  obtain ⟨hfi, hlt⟩ := StratonovichHAMAudit.ClockFilter.strict_filter_integral θ hθ L0
   752	    (by simp) ae_L0_pos (weight alpha0 θ μ) hwi
   753	    (ae_L0_pos.mono fun l hl => weight_pos μ hR hμ alpha0 θ l ha0 hθ hl)
   754	  refine ⟨fun l hl => weight_pos μ hR hμ alpha0 θ l ha0 hθ hl, hwi,
   755	    N2_outer_integrable μ hR alpha0 θ ha0 ha1 hθ, hK, hJi, hJ1i, hJpos, hJle, hfi, hJ1, ?_, ?_⟩
   756	  · rw [hJ1, hK]
   757	    exact hlt
   758	  · intro h1
   759	    subst h1
   760	    exact degree_one μ hR hμ0 hI alpha0 θ ha0 ha1 hθ
   761	
   762	/-- The nonnegativity `N₂(θ)² ≥ 0` of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` under
   763	`H:homog` (no `Γ ≠ 0` needed) and the supplied spectral homogeneity, as a
   764	corollary of `N₂(θ)² = ∫ w_θ` (the TeX argues by positive definiteness of the
   765	temporal kernel). -/
   766	theorem damped_N2_nonneg_paper {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   767	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha)
   768	    (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) : 0 ≤ N2sq alpha0 θ μ := by
   769	  have := h.μ_radon
   770	  have hα0 : 0 < alpha := by
   771	    rcases h.alpha_range with h1 | h1
   772	    · exact h1.1
   773	    · rw [h1.1, h1.2]; norm_num
   774	  have hR := integrable_inv_one_add_sq hI (by linarith [h.threshold, h.alpha0_pos])
   775	  rw [K_eq_integral_weight μ hR (measure_zero hI hα0) alpha0 θ h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one hθ]
   776	  exact setIntegral_nonneg measurableSet_Ioi fun l hl =>
   777	    weight_nonneg μ hR alpha0 θ l h.alpha0_pos hθ hl
   778	
   779	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.ClockCopy

699	## ClockCopy (whole result)
   700	
   701	Formalizes `P:clock-copy-obstruction`
   702	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `975feb3`, lines
   703	7681-7831) in full, with its displays `E:cross-clock-lambda-weight`,
   704	`E:clock-copy-obstruction` and `E:degree-one-clock-loss`, together with the
   705	finiteness part of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lines 766-846) and
   706	`N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`. The module `ClockCopy` rests on four foundation
   707	modules of the D4 layer (Fourier and Laplace analysis of the wave kernel
   708	and the time kernel), whose rows are marked "[D4 foundation: <Module>]":
   709	`WaveKernel` (`G_s hat` as `waveHat s xi = s sinc(s|xi|)`, which is
   710	`sin(s|xi|)/|xi|` with value `s` at `0`; its bounds, scaling and Laplace
   711	transform), `TimeFractional` (subordination
   712	`r^(-a) = Gamma(a)^(-1) int l^(a-1) e^(-r l) dl`, the kernel `Psi_a` of
   713	`E:averaged-clock-kernel` and its properties, and the two-time Laplace
   714	lemma `int int e^(-as-bt-lam|s-t|) = (a+b+2lam)/((a+b)(a+lam)(b+lam))` for
   715	complex `a, b` with positive real part), `SpectralHomog` (consequences of
   716	the spectral homogeneity, `R_Gamma`, `h_Gamma`, and `Gamma != 0 => mu != 0`)
   717	and `DampedNorms` (`N_1`, `N_2^2` of `E:damped-norm-definitions` and their
   718	finiteness). `H:homog` is `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance` with temporal
   719	exponent `a = alpha0`; the wrappers `clock_copy_obstruction_paper`,
   720	`damped_norms_finite_paper` and `damped_N2_nonneg_paper` state the results
   721	with the manuscript's hypotheses (`Gamma != 0`, `theta > 0`,
   722	`-1 <= rho <= 1` for the proposition; `Gamma != 0` is not assumed for the
   723	lemma). These wrappers take ONE further input as an argument:
   724	`SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha`, `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)` for Borel `A` and
   725	`c > 0`, which the TeX derives from the scaling of `Gamma` and Fourier
   726	uniqueness in the proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lines 795-796; the
   727	same derivation is in the proof of `L:low-alpha-convolution`, lines
   728	4645-4649). This input is now derived under `H:homog` by
   729	`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, and
   730	`ClockCopyHomog.clock_copy_obstruction_paper`,
   731	`ClockCopyHomog.damped_norms_finite_paper` and
   732	`ClockCopyHomog.damped_N2_nonneg_paper` state the three results with
   733	nothing supplied (see "MaskedSpectralGrowth (whole result)"); the
   734	statements of this section are unchanged. Its consequences
   735	`mu{0} = 0`, `mu(B_r) = r^alpha mu(B_1)`, `int (1+|xi|^2)^(-1) dmu < inf`
   736	(by the layer-cake formula), and the homogeneity of `R_Gamma` and `h_Gamma`
   737	are proved; Lebesgue measure on `R^1` satisfies the input (see
   738	`refutations/clock-copy/WrongDegreeOneConstant.lean`). Implicit hypotheses
   739	made explicit: integrals over `(0,inf)` and `(0,inf)^2` are Bochner
   740	integrals for Lebesgue measure (`TimeFractional.L0`, `TimeFractional.P2`).
   741	Since the Lean integral of a non-integrable function is `0`, every integral
   742	the paper asserts to be finite (`w_theta`, the `N_1` and `N_2` integrands,
   743	the outer integrand of `N_2^2`, the `J` integrands and `2 theta/(2 theta +
   744	l) w_theta`) comes with a proved integrability conclusion; the auxiliary
   745	scaling identities `SpectralHomog.integral_comp_smul` (measurable `f` only)
   746	and `ClockCopy.integral_rpow_div_add_scaling` (`c > 0` only, any `a`) are
   747	identities of Lean's totalized integrals with no integrability conclusion,
   748	and are used only where integrability is proved separately
   749	(`ClockCopy.integrable_rpow_div_add` needs `0 < a < 1`). `G_s hat` is real,
   750	so the complex conjugate in `N_2` is dropped. `Psi_a(theta|u-v|, .)` and
   751	`|s-t|^(-a)` take Lean's junk values on the diagonal, a null set (the TeX
   752	notes the diagonal is irrelevant). Hypotheses carried but unused: in
   753	`clock_copy_obstruction_paper`, `rho >= -1` and the fields `dim`,
   754	`Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `mu_tempered`
   755	and the `Gamma` scaling of `HomogCovariance` (the latter replaced by the
   756	supplied input); in `damped_norms_finite_paper`, the fields `dim`,
   757	`Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`,
   758	`mu_tempered`, `spectral`, the `Gamma` scaling and `alpha_range`; in

   760	`Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral` and
   761	the `Gamma` scaling. The `ClockCopyHomog` wrappers use `mu_tempered`,
   762	`spectral` and the `Gamma` scaling to derive the input. The proof route differs from the TeX, though the
   763	statements do not. On the `K` side Lean does not smooth the covariance and
   764	pass to a monotone limit: it expands `|s-t|^(-a)` by subordination and
   765	applies Fubini on `(0,inf) x R^d x (0,inf)^2`, justified by an absolute
   766	majorant built from `|G_s hat G_t hat| <= 2(1+s)(1+t)/(1+|xi|^2)`. This is
   767	a different route, not the one after "Alternatively" in the TeX (lines

  2042	Formalizes `P:masked-spectral-growth` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex`
  2043	at `975feb3`, lines 34-77) in full, with its displays
  2044	`E:masked-gaussian-transform` (lines 42-45) and `E:masked-translated-ball`
  2045	(lines 46-49). It also derives the spectral homogeneity

  2047	`ClockCopy` take as their one supplied input. The TeX derives it from the
